about.title: Covina Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Covina's stretch of San Gabriel Valley roadways carries a steady mix of local traffic and commuters cutting through on Citrus Avenue and San Bernardino Road. Public records show 117 injury collisions and 165 injured people in the most recent final crash year, with Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the heaviest concentration of reported crashes. Behind each of those numbers is a person dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who may call before the dust even settles. LawProactive doesn't practice law—we're a free service that connects injured Covina residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of your crash. Los Angeles County traffic can move fast at intersections along these corridors, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness memory fades quickly. Getting matched with someone who understands local roads and California claims can help you avoid early mistakes.

whyChoose.title: Why Covina Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Your Time Window Is Limited
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Connecting with an attorney early helps make sure that deadline doesn't slip by unnoticed.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you're found partly responsible for the crash—your recovery is simply adjusted to reflect your share. An attorney can help make sure your percentage of fault isn't overstated by the other side.

items.title: No Recorded Statement, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often want a recorded statement early, which can be used against you later—an attorney can speak for you instead. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you actually recover money.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash near Grand Avenue and Badillo Street—what should I do first?
items.answer: Seek medical care first, even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms surface days later. Try to document the scene with photos if you're able, and avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer. From there, getting connected with an independent attorney can help preserve evidence before it disappears.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Covina car accident?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That window shortens significantly, sometimes to six months, if a government entity or vehicle was involved. Because these deadlines are strict, it's wise to get guidance sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if the insurance company says I was partly at fault?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you share some blame for the crash. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't eliminated. An attorney can push back if the insurer tries to inflate your share unfairly.
